stories.title: Android Auto and Android Automotive: What Sets Them Apart
stories.summary: Engadget published an explainer on Google's two in-car software platforms. Android Auto projects a phone's interface onto a car's screen. Android Automotive is a full operating system built into the vehicle itself.
stories.whyItMatters: Automakers increasingly build software directly into cars, and the similar names create real confusion for buyers and industry watchers alike.
whatToWatch: More automakers adopting Android Automotive as a built-in system

stories.title: Is Training AI on Copyrighted Books Legal? It's Complicated
stories.summary: TechCrunch examines the unsettled legal question of whether AI companies can train models on copyrighted books. Courts are actively working through the issue, and the answer varies by case and jurisdiction.
stories.whyItMatters: The outcome will shape how AI companies source training data and could reset the economics between publishers, authors, and AI firms.
whatToWatch: Pending court rulings on AI training and copyright
New lawsuits from authors or publishers
questions: Will courts settle on one consistent fair-use standard?

stories.title: Who Built the Mystery 'Stealth Model' Ox Alpha?
stories.summary: TechCrunch investigates the origin of an unidentified new AI model called Ox Alpha. The model appeared without a disclosed creator, a pattern known as a stealth release used to test models before an official announcement.
stories.whyItMatters: Stealth releases raise questions about transparency and accountability among AI labs racing to ship new models.
whatToWatch: Confirmation of who built Ox Alpha
